proof: Emulation asks: how do we reproduce this old machine? Retro Porting Toolkit asks a different question: what could its games do if they were not limited by that machine anymore?

Traditional emulators recreate the original hardware extremely well, and this project builds on decades of that accumulated knowledge. But by recompiling games back into real code and recovering how they actually work, the toolkit operates above the hardware abstraction. Changes become possible at the level of the game itself.

A remaster is a new commercial production. A source port needs source code or a heroic reverse-engineering effort for one title. An emulator reproduces the machine. Retro Porting Toolkit occupies another space entirely: preserve the game, replace the constraints. The goal is not to make old games unrecognizable. It is to make the boundaries around them programmable.

items.text: Notebookcheck on Pepsiman in the browser

philosophy: Go native. Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, even the browser. No emulator core in sight.
See more of the world. Adaptive widescreen up to 21:9 in games like Tomba! 2 and Mega Man Zero.
Break the old limits. 60 FPS patches, CD-quality MSU-1 soundtracks, voxel 3D remixes, and mod loaders that never touch your original ROM.
Swap the hardware. Spin WarioWare: Twisted! with your phone or a DualSense, and let real local weather drive Boktai's solar sensor.
Change the words. Runtime text replacement powers Tsumu Light's English fan translation and NES text overrides.
Play together. Shared netplay, rollback, save states, and rewind (recomp-net and retcomm-rbengine) that every ecosystem can pick up.

capabilities.title: Higher frame rates
capabilities.body: Run games smoothly beyond their original frame-rate limits.

capabilities.title: Modern displays
capabilities.body: Widescreen, ultrawide, high-resolution output, and flexible viewports.

capabilities.title: Modern multiplayer
capabilities.body: Turn local multiplayer and console link modes into LAN and online play.

capabilities.title: Modding
capabilities.body: Expose game data and behavior for characters, assets, rules, levels, and entirely new experiences.

pillars.title: Recompile
pillars.body: Translate original game code into code that runs efficiently on modern hardware, without manually rewriting the game.

pillars.title: Understand
pillars.body: Recover higher-level knowledge about the game's code, data, assets, and systems, so the toolkit knows what the running game actually means.

pillars.title: Augment
pillars.body: Use that knowledge to replace or extend individual systems with modern implementations: rendering, input, networking, audio, storage, UI.

thesis: A traditional port improves one game. Retro Porting Toolkit is designed to improve the platform underneath many games.

Teach the toolkit how a PlayStation game establishes a display, and a whole class of games can inherit modern display modes. Implement modern handling for a common input path, and many games pick up modern controllers at once. Understand a console's link protocol, and games designed around two physical consoles can meet over a network instead.
Every game teaches the toolkit more about its platform. Every platform improvement makes the next game easier. The toolkit gets better; the library gets bigger.

transforms.title: Split screen becomes multiple displays
transforms.body: A game already knows how to render two players. Give each player their own viewport, window, or monitor.

transforms.title: Link cable becomes network play
transforms.body: Some PlayStation games connected two consoles with a serial cable. Reimplement the transport, and the same game logic can travel over LAN or the internet while the game still believes it is talking to another PlayStation.

transforms.title: Controller port becomes modern input
transforms.body: Map the original input model onto contemporary controllers, keyboard and mouse, or accessibility hardware.

transforms.title: Fixed viewport becomes widescreen
transforms.body: Understand how the game builds its camera and projection instead of stretching the final image.
